description: Add support for image and voice messages from Telegram and iMessage channels. Images should be passed to vision models and voice messages should be transcribed (e.g. via Whisper) before reaching the agent. Currently only text messages are processed.

userStories.title: Message model extension with media attachments
userStories.description: Extend the Channel callback interface and ChatServer.handle_message to support media attachments alongside text.
acceptanceCriteria: New dataclass or Pydantic model: IncomingMessage with fields: sender_id (str), text (str | None), attachments (list[Attachment]), channel (str | None)

Attachment model with fields: type (enum: image, voice, audio, video, file), file_path (Path | None), url (str | None), mime_type (str | None), file_name (str | None), file_size (int | None), data (bytes | None)
These models live in src/taskrunner/channels/message.py (new file)
Channel.listen callback signature updated: Callable[[IncomingMessage], str] — the old (sender_id, text) signature still works via a compatibility wrapper
ChatServer.handle_message accepts optional attachments parameter: handle_message(sender_id, text, ..., attachments=None)
When attachments are present, they're stored in the message context for the LLM to access
Backward compatible: channels that don't support media still work with plain text
All existing tests pass
userStories.notes: The Channel base class callback is Callable[[str, str], str]. We need a backward-compatible migration. Consider a new callback type that accepts IncomingMessage but wrap old-style (sender_id, text) callbacks. ChatServer.handle_message is in src/taskrunner/chat.py line 114. DaemonService._handle_message in src/taskrunner/daemon/service.py bridges channels to ChatServer.

userStories.title: Media storage and file management
userStories.description: Create a media storage service that saves incoming media files to a local directory with organized naming.
acceptanceCriteria: New service: src/taskrunner/services/media_store.py
MediaStore class with configurable base directory (default: ~/.creel/media/)
save_media(attachment: Attachment, sender_id: str) -> Path: saves file to disk, returns path
File organization: ~/.creel/media/{channel}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{uuid}.{ext}
Deduplication: if identical file already saved (by content hash), return existing path
Cleanup method: remove files older than N days (configurable, default 30)
Supports saving from bytes (data field), file path (copy/move), or URL (download)
For URL downloads: use httpx with timeout and max file size (20MB default)
Returns the saved file path for downstream processing
Unit tests for save/retrieve/cleanup
userStories.notes: Keep it simple — local filesystem storage. No cloud/S3. The media directory should be created on first use.

userStories.title: Voice transcription service
userStories.description: Service to transcribe voice messages to text using OpenAI Whisper API or local whisper.
acceptanceCriteria: New service: src/taskrunner/services/transcription.py
TranscriptionService class with two backends: 'openai' (API) and 'local' (whisper CLI)
transcribe(file_path: Path) -> str: returns transcribed text
OpenAI backend: uses the OpenAI Whisper API (POST to /v1/audio/transcriptions with the audio file)
Uses the existing LLM API key from agent config (OpenAI key) — or a separate WHISPER_API_KEY env var
Local backend: shells out to 'whisper' CLI if installed, falls back to OpenAI API
Supports common audio formats: .ogg, .opus, .m4a, .mp3, .wav, .oga
For Telegram voice: handles .oga/.ogg Opus files (Telegram's voice format)
For iMessage voice: handles .caf/.m4a files (macOS voice message format)
Configurable in agent.yaml under media.transcription: {backend: 'openai', model: 'whisper-1'}
Returns empty string with warning log if transcription fails (don't crash the agent)
Unit tests with mocked API calls
userStories.notes: Most users will use the OpenAI API. The local whisper fallback is nice-to-have. For the OpenAI API, POST multipart/form-data to https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions with model=whisper-1. The existing LLMConfig has api_key — reuse it if provider is openai.

userStories.title: Vision processing service
userStories.description: Service to process images for LLM vision models, converting them to the right format for the agent's LLM provider.
acceptanceCriteria: New service: src/taskrunner/services/vision.py
VisionProcessor class
prepare_image(file_path: Path) -> dict: returns a content block suitable for the LLM provider
For OpenAI-compatible APIs: returns {type: 'image_url', image_url: {url: 'data:image/jpeg;base64,...'}}
For Anthropic: returns {type: 'image', source: {type: 'base64', media_type: '...', data: '...'}}
Auto-detects image format from file extension or magic bytes
Resizes images larger than 2048px on longest side (using Pillow) to reduce token usage
Converts unsupported formats (HEIC, WEBP) to JPEG
Configurable max image size in agent.yaml under media.vision: {max_pixels: 2048, quality: 85}
Returns None with warning log for unsupported/corrupt files
Pillow added as optional dependency (with helpful error if missing)
Unit tests for format detection, resizing, base64 encoding
userStories.notes: Check src/taskrunner/chat.py to see how messages are built for the LLM. The LLM provider info is in AgentConfig.llm.provider. Support at least 'openai' and 'anthropic' content block formats.

userStories.title: iMessage channel media support
userStories.description: Extend the existing iMessage channel to handle image and voice message attachments from chat.db.
acceptanceCriteria: IMessageChannel._poll now also queries the attachment table in chat.db
SQL join: message_attachment_join + attachment tables to get attachment paths
For image attachments (mime_type starts with 'image/'): create Attachment with file_path pointing to ~/Library/Messages/Attachments/... path
For voice/audio attachments (mime_type starts with 'audio/'): create Attachment with file_path, type=voice
Incoming messages with attachments create IncomingMessage with both text and attachments populated
Image attachments: copied to media store (don't reference Messages/Attachments directly as it may be cleaned up)
Voice attachments (.caf files): copied to media store, then transcribed
The listen callback receives the full IncomingMessage with attachments
Handle edge cases: attachment file missing from disk, unsupported mime types
Backward compatible: text-only messages still work exactly as before
Tests for attachment query SQL, message construction
userStories.notes: chat.db schema: message table has ROWID, attachment table has ROWID + filename + mime_type + transfer_name, message_attachment_join links them (message_id, attachment_id). Attachment filename field contains the full path like ~/Library/Messages/Attachments/XX/YY/uuid/filename.ext. The ~ needs to be expanded. Voice messages from iMessage are typically .caf format.

userStories.title: Agent message building with vision and transcription
userStories.description: Update ChatServer to build LLM messages that include image content blocks and prepend transcribed voice text.
acceptanceCriteria: ChatServer.handle_message processes attachments before sending to LLM
Voice attachments: transcribed text is prepended to the user message as '[Voice message]: {transcribed_text}'
Image attachments: VisionProcessor.prepare_image() output is added to the LLM message content blocks
For OpenAI-style providers: message content becomes an array of content blocks [{type: 'text', text: '...'}, {type: 'image_url', ...}]
For Anthropic: message content becomes an array [{type: 'text', text: '...'}, {type: 'image', source: {...}}]
Multiple images in one message: all added as separate content blocks
Voice + image in same message: both processed (transcription + vision)
If transcription fails: message sent as '[Voice message: transcription failed]' with the audio file path noted
If vision processing fails: message sent as '[Image attached but could not be processed]'
MediaStore, TranscriptionService, and VisionProcessor are initialized in ChatServer.__init__ based on agent config
All existing tests pass, new tests for multi-modal message building
userStories.notes: Check how ChatServer builds messages for the LLM — look at the _build_messages or similar method in chat.py. The LLM provider determines the content block format. Key: the message 'content' field changes from a string to a list of content blocks when images are present.

userStories.title: Agent config for media settings
acceptanceCriteria: New config section in agent.yaml: media: {enabled: true, storage_dir: ~/.creel/media, max_file_size_mb: 20, retention_days: 30, transcription: {backend: openai, model: whisper-1, api_key: null}, vision: {max_pixels: 2048, quality: 85}}
MediaConfig Pydantic model in src/taskrunner/models.py with all fields, sensible defaults
AgentConfig gets optional media: MediaConfig | None field
When media is None or media.enabled is false: attachments are ignored with a log message, text-only processing continues
TranscriptionService reads api_key from media.transcription.api_key, falling back to llm.api_key
Config is passed to MediaStore, TranscriptionService, VisionProcessor on init
Default agent.yaml template includes media section (commented out with examples)
Existing configs without media section continue to work (backward compatible)
Tests for config parsing with and without media section
userStories.notes: Add to the existing model hierarchy in models.py. Keep defaults sensible so it works out of the box for OpenAI users — they just need media.enabled: true since api_key falls back to the LLM key.

userStories.title: End-to-end Telegram image flow
userStories.description: Verify the complete flow: user sends image in Telegram → bot downloads → vision model processes → agent responds about the image.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: simulate a Telegram webhook with a photo message
Photo is downloaded from Telegram API (mocked), saved to media store
Image is processed by VisionProcessor and added to LLM content blocks
LLM receives the image and generates a response about it (mocked LLM)
Response is sent back to the Telegram chat via sendMessage
Media file exists on disk at ~/.creel/media/telegram/{date}/{uuid}.jpg
Full flow test from webhook receipt to response delivery
userStories.notes: Telegram channel already exists at src/taskrunner/channels/telegram.py with telegram_bridge.py. TelegramAttachment model has file_id, file_type, mime_type, file_name. Bridge has download_file(file_id) -> bytes. Build on this existing infrastructure.

userStories.title: End-to-end Telegram voice flow
userStories.description: Verify the complete flow: user sends voice message in Telegram → bot downloads → Whisper transcribes → agent responds.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: simulate a Telegram webhook with a voice message
Voice .oga file downloaded from Telegram API (mocked), saved to media store
Audio transcribed by TranscriptionService (mocked Whisper API returns 'Hello, this is a test')
Transcribed text prepended to message: '[Voice message]: Hello, this is a test'
LLM receives the text and generates a response (mocked)
Response sent back to Telegram chat
Full flow from webhook to response
userStories.notes: Same as MEDIA-009 but for voice. Telegram voice messages come as file_type="voice" in TelegramAttachment. Use existing bridge.download_file() to get the .oga bytes.

userStories.title: End-to-end iMessage image flow
userStories.description: Verify the complete flow: user sends image via iMessage → chat.db poll picks it up → vision processes → agent responds.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: mock chat.db with an image attachment row
Attachment file path resolved from ~/Library/Messages/Attachments/...
Image copied to media store, processed by VisionProcessor
LLM receives image content block and generates response (mocked)
Response sent back via AppleScript (mocked)
Test handles missing attachment file gracefully (file cleaned up by macOS)
userStories.notes: iMessage attachments are trickier because the file paths in chat.db may use ~ and the files may be cleaned up by macOS. Test the path resolution and missing-file handling.

userStories.title: End-to-end iMessage voice flow
userStories.description: Verify the complete flow: user sends voice message via iMessage → chat.db poll → transcription → agent responds.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: mock chat.db with a voice/audio attachment row (.caf mime type)
Audio file copied to media store, transcribed via TranscriptionService
Transcribed text prepended to message
LLM receives text and generates response (mocked)
Response sent back via AppleScript (mocked)
Handle .caf format: if Whisper doesn't support .caf directly, convert to .wav or .m4a first using ffmpeg (with fallback if ffmpeg not installed)
userStories.notes: iMessage voice messages are .caf (Core Audio Format). OpenAI Whisper API supports: flac, m4a, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, oga, ogg, wav, webm. CAF is NOT in the list — so we need ffmpeg conversion. Add a convert_audio() helper that uses ffmpeg if available, otherwise logs a warning.
